name: Denise Biellmann
milestone_by_age_26: Won the 1981 World Figure Skating Championships and the 1981 European Championships at age 18, becoming the first and only Swiss woman to win the World title.
early_history_summary: Born in Zurich, Biellmann was on the ice at age 3 at the Dolder rink, coached by her mother Heidi, herself a figure skater. She won her first international competition at age 8, was Swiss Junior champion at 11, landed the first triple Lutz by a woman in competition at 15, and won European and World titles at 18.
family_context_summary: Born in Zurich to Heidi Biellmann, herself a figure skater who became Denise's coach throughout her amateur and professional career. Her mother traveled to all competitions with her and maintained an extremely close relationship.
parent_family_domain_summary: Mother Heidi Biellmann was a figure skater who coached Denise from age 3 through her entire career, providing direct domain expertise and sustained individualized training.
primary_early_advantage_tags: mother as coach, early ice access, prodigy, triple Lutz pioneer, Biellmann Spin
evidence_summary: Biellmann was born in Zurich and was on the ice at age 3 at the Dolder rink, where her mother Heidi — herself a figure skater — quickly recognized her talent and became her coach. She won her first international competition at age 8, was Swiss Junior champion at 11, and at age 15 became the first woman to land a triple Lutz in competition. At 18, she won both the European and World Championships, becoming the first and only Swiss woman to win the World title. The Biellmann Spin, which she developed and popularized, is now part of the ISU Judging System.
starting_point: Born in Zurich, Switzerland to Heidi Biellmann, a figure skater who became her coach; was on the ice at age 3 at the Dolder rink in Zurich.
current_position: Active as a figure skating coach and occasional performer in Switzerland; coaches competitive athletes and junior skaters at the Dolder ice rink in Zurich; was voted Swiss Sportswoman of the Century in 1995.
